instruction_bucket.subject: CHEMISTRY
instruction_bucket.title: Track species, oxidation state, electron consequence and agent role

research_questions: Which misconceptions recur around oxidation number, ionic charge and electron transfer?
Which representations help learners preserve species identity while moving from reaction equation to oxidation-state reasoning?
How should explanation and learner-generated reconstruction be sequenced to avoid unnecessary cognitive load?

governing_rules: Track the same element or species before assigning a Redox label.
An increase in oxidation state is oxidation; a decrease is reduction.
SELF change is evidence; the agent role is the conclusion.
Oxidation state is a bookkeeping value; do not automatically treat it as an isolated-particle charge.
The electron loss and gain represented here must balance: 2e- lost = 2e- gained.

research_evidence.design_use: Add explicit contrasts for oxidation number versus charge, electron transfer and overconfident wrong models.
Include diagnosis of recurring oxidation-number/charge and oxidation/reduction misconceptions.
Use representation bridges deliberately, but preserve the upstream Redox restriction to symbolic representation for this bucket instead of adding unauthorized particle imagery.
Move from explicit reconstruction frames toward completion, fading and independent teach-back rather than repeating full worked solutions.
